articles.title: Researchers demonstrate prompt injection through document metadata
articles.author: jonas-weber
articles.summary: Researchers show that instructions hidden in document metadata can influence AI assistants that summarise files.
articles.imageAlt: Editorial illustration for ai story: AI Security

brief.what: Researchers show that instructions hidden in document metadata can influence AI assistants that summarise files.
brief.who: Assistants with access to email, files or actions are most at risk.
brief.why: Assistants that can take actions or access sensitive data face the greatest risk.
brief.next: The researchers disclosed findings to affected vendors before publication.

articles.whyItMatters: Assistants that can take actions or access sensitive data face the greatest risk. Treat all retrieved content as untrusted, limit tool permissions and log model actions for review.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Researchers show that instructions hidden in document metadata can influence AI assistants that summarise files.
The instructions are invisible in normal document views but are read by the model.

sections.heading: Technical Analysis
paragraphs: Prompt injection occurs when untrusted content is interpreted by a model as instructions.
Hidden text in document metadata or formatting can carry instructions that users never see.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Assistants that can take actions or access sensitive data face the greatest risk.
Assistants with access to email, files or actions are most at risk.

sections.heading: What you should know
paragraphs: Treat all retrieved content as untrusted, limit tool permissions and log model actions for review.
The researchers disclosed findings to affected vendors before publication.
